established_findings.statement: LLMs and agentic LLM systems are actively applied to NetOps/AIOps tasks (intent-to-configuration translation, incident summarization, agentic network-management prototypes) and show promise in prototype and research settings.
established_findings.evidence_type: mixed (empirical system papers, prototypes, and surveys)
limitations: Most reported results are prototypes or controlled evaluations rather than large-scale production deployments.
Tasks and datasets used in these works are heterogeneous and often narrow in scope.

established_findings.statement: Hallucination (factually unsupported or incorrect outputs) is a prominent and well-documented failure mode of LLMs; detection/mitigation strategies (RAG, ensembles, self-reflection, abductive checks) reduce but do not eliminate such failures.
limitations: Mitigation effectiveness varies by domain, evaluation metric, and dataset; none guarantee elimination of hallucination.
Few studies evaluate these methods specifically on NetOps configuration-generation end-to-end.

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented LLM agents (invoking external tools, domain solvers, or verification components) demonstrably improve task correctness and robustness in multiple domains; this pattern is proposed as a promising mitigation direction for high-stakes automation.
established_findings.evidence_type: empirical agent/system papers and engineering reports
limitations: Most empirical demonstrations are in non-networking domains or prototypes; NetOps-specific tool integrations remain less-explored.
Tool integration increases system complexity, latency, and engineering effort.

established_findings.statement: The literature documents scarcity of public supervision data and tailored benchmarks for network-configuration translation and verification, limiting reproducible evaluation of LLM-based NetOps approaches.
established_findings.evidence_type: system paper and survey noting dataset/benchmark gaps
limitations: Absence claim is based on surveyed literature in these sources; other undiscovered datasets may exist.
Some projects create private corpora or task-specific corpora not publicly released.

unresolved_questions.statement: Can composing LLM generation with deterministic network-verification (generate–validate–repair) produce end-to-end safety levels adequate for automated configuration deployment in operational networks?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: proposal/prototype papers and agent survey (not full empirical NetOps verifier–LLM studies)
limitations: Provided records propose or motivate such pipelines but do not present large-scale, production-grade empirical evaluations demonstrating operational safety.
Concrete composition with canonical network verifiers and deployment studies are not present among the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent does human-in-the-loop oversight reliably prevent automation-induced incidents in NetOps, versus serving primarily as liability/approval ritual?
limitations: Evidence includes theoretical critique and cross-domain surveys rather than controlled NetOps field experiments measuring HITL effectiveness.
Human oversight effectiveness likely depends on workflow design, operator incentives, and time pressure—factors not uniformly studied.

unresolved_questions.statement: Which evaluation metrics and protocols most validly capture operational correctness, safety, and trustworthiness for LLM-driven NetOps agents?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: survey and system paper noting evaluation/benchmarking gaps
limitations: Surveys identify the gap but do not converge on a standardized metric suite specific to NetOps safety.
Designing metrics that map to real operational risk requires access to deployment traces and incident data absent in these sources.

candidate_gaps.statement: Create standardized public NetOps datasets and benchmarks that target operational correctness, verifier-groundedness, and safety properties (e.g., ACL/BGP/ACL semantics, intended policy preservation) for LLM evaluation.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: system paper and survey identifying dataset/benchmark scarcity
limitations: Feasibility depends on data sharing constraints and anonymization of operator artifacts.
Benchmark design must avoid superficial proxies and target operationally meaningful failure modes.

candidate_gaps.statement: Conduct empirical NetOps-specific evaluations of generate–validate–repair pipelines that compose LLMs with deterministic network validators across realistic topologies and failure-injection scenarios.
limitations: Existing evidence shows promise of tool-augmentation in other domains but lacks NetOps end-to-end empirical studies in the supplied records.
Such experiments require careful preregistration and operational realism to be convincing.

candidate_gaps.statement: Investigate prompt-coupling and prompt-sensitivity for NetOps templates and cross-model robustness to support multi-vendor, multi-model deployments of intent-to-config systems.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: conceptual/method papers on prompt coupling and prompt-engineering survey
limitations: Prompt coupling work is conceptual and nascent; empirical NetOps-focused prompt-sensitivity studies are required.
Cross-model compilation solutions introduce engineering complexity and may not generalize across vendor-specific CLIs.

excluded_claims: LLMs are production-ready to perform fully autonomous NetOps configuration changes without human oversight (unsupported by supplied records).
RAG or a single mitigation method fully eliminates hallucination or misconfiguration risk in operational NetOps contexts (no supplied record proves complete elimination).
The supplied literature contains empirical evidence that verifier–LLM pipelines have been validated at production scale to prevent all misconfigurations (not supported by provided records).
